title: Operator Autoscaler Feedback Loop Retrospective
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
-------

This retrospective documents a series of incidents in Q4 2025 and early Q1 2026 where the operator-tier autoscaler introduced a feedback loop that caused repeated token-surge-induced scaling oscillations for several multitenant GPU pools. The oscillations increased p99 latencies, caused SLA burn, and generated significant operational toil. This doc explains timeline, root causes, mitigations performed, permanent fixes, monitoring changes, and a rollout checklist to avoid recurrence.

Impact and metrics
------------------

- Affected services: runtime-serving-llm, tenant-scheduler, operator-autoscaler
- Customer-visible impact window: 2025-11-03 03:12 UTC — 2026-01-18 21:40 UTC (intermittent spikes)
- Measured effects (example aggregate across 3 impacted GPU pools):
  - p95 request latency: +18% average during surge events
  - p99 request latency: +42% (worst week)
  - Token throughput variance: +/- 38% minute-to-minute
  - Autoscaler churn: average 4 scale actions/hour during bursts (desired <= 0.5/hr)
  - Operator on-call interrupts: 38 pages over 10 incidents

Timeline (high level)
--------------------

1. Nov 3 2025: First operator pages from regional oncall for pool-3 showing rapid scale-outs followed by immediate scale-ins.
2. Nov 4-10: Initial mitigations applied: increased stabilization window, raised min-replicas. Churn slowed but returned.
3. Dec 12: Canary rollout of autoscaler v1.5 introduced a heuristic that aggressively scales based on short-term token rate forecasts.
4. Dec 18–Jan 12: Multiple rolling oscillations coincident with tenant token surges (marketing-driven user spikes); autoscaler reacted too quickly, then evicted workloads, which triggered retries and more surges.
5. Jan 13: Emergency manual override to pin scale to safe capacity for impacted pools.
6. Jan 18: Root cause analysis complete, permanent mitigations scheduled.

Root causes
-----------

- Short-term forecasting heuristic in autoscaler v1.5 used a rolling 15s window and a naive extrapolation factor (x2) without dampening, making the control loop underdamped for bursty LLM workloads.
- Eviction policy triggered on scale-in when memory footprint briefly exceeded the target; evictions caused request retries which amplified token-rate transiently.
- Metrics used by the autoscaler (tokens/sec) were sampled at coarse Prometheus scrape intervals (15s) with aggregation that lost burst peak shape; combined with the heuristic this produced overconfidence in forecasted demand.
- Lack of a stabilization policy scoped to tenant categories (i.e., bursty marketing tenants vs stable API tenants).
- Insufficient alerting for oscillatory behavior (we alerted on scale actions but not on action-rate per time window or on upstream retries triggered by evictions).

Immediate mitigations applied
---------------------------

1. Reverted autoscaler to v1.4 on 2025-12-20 for all production pools to remove aggressive forecasting heuristic. (Owner: infra-autoscale team)
2. Applied a temporary global stabilization window: require 90s sustained change before scale-in; scale-out kept at 30s guard.
3. Pinned eviction policy to favor soft-eviction (throttling) for 72 hours after scale events.
4. Increased min-replicas for high-variability pools (pool-2, pool-3).
5. Added an ad-hoc dashboard and runbook for operators to observe: scale-action-rate, eviction-rate, retry-rate, tokens/sec 5s/30s.

Why the initial mitigation was insufficient
-----------------------------------------

- Reverts reduced immediate oscillation but did not give a durable design change: the underlying telemetry and policy mismatch remained.
- Existing dashboards surfaced per-action counts but did not visualize the control loop phase/lag, which made tuning blind.

Permanent remediation work (accepted design)
------------------------------------------

Design summary (approved Feb 2026): replace the naive short-window forecast with a multi-timescale controller and tenant-aware stabilization rules. High-level components:

- Multi-timescale demand estimator: compute tokens/sec at 5s, 30s, and 5min windows; use a conservative compose function: demand = max(smoothed(5s) * 1.15, smoothed(30s)*1.05, smoothed(5m)).
- Dampened control law: introduce PI-like term with capped derivative contribution to eliminate overshoot for short bursts.
- Tenant profiles: label tenants as BURSTY, STEADY, or LATENT in tenant-metadata service; different stabilization windows and min-replicas per profile.
- Eviction policy change: soft-eviction-first, prefer request-level shedding and token-throttling over immediate pod eviction; escalate to hard-eviction only if memory pressure persists > 60s after shedding.
- Observability: new control-loop health SLI and dashboard, plus synthetic canary workload to exercise the loop.

Ownership and timeline
----------------------

- Design owner: infra-autoscale team (lead: Diego Alvarez)
- Runtime changes: eng-serving-runtime (kernel) and infra-autoscale (controller) — coordinated rollout.
- Observability: eng-platform/dashboards (owner: Priya Nair)
- Tenant profiling and metadata service: product-platform (owner: Evan Brooks)

Planned rollout milestones:
1) Mar 2026: Implement multi-timescale estimator behind feature flag; unit and integration tests.
2) Apr 2026: Deploy to staging and run 2-week synthetic canary; collect metrics.
3) May 2026: Gradual rollout to non-critical pools with A/B monitoring.
4) Jun 2026: Full rollout and deprecation of feature flag.

Dashboard and alerting changes (concrete)
---------------------------------------

New dashboards (owner: eng-platform/dashboards):
- Autoscaler-control-loop-overview: shows tokens/sec 5s/30s/5m, estimator output, desired_replicas, actual_replicas, derivative_term, and active_feature_flags.
- Oscillation-forensics: scale-action-rate (per-minute), eviction-rate, retry-rate, average backoff time, tenant-token-variance heatmap.

Proposed alerts (thresholds are initial suggestions):
1. Alert: autoscaler_oscillation_rate_high
   - Expr: rate(autoscaler_scale_actions_total[5m]) > 2
   - For: 3m
   - Severity: page
   - Runbook: confirm whether evictions correlate with scale-ins; if yes, pin scale and notify infra-autoscale.
2. Alert: eviction_retry_amplification
   - Expr: increase(evictions_total[5m]) > 10 and rate(retries_total[5m]) > 50
   - For: 1m
   - Severity: page
   - Runbook: temporarily set soft-eviction-only and increase min-replicas; open incident if sustained.
3. Alert: control_loop_derivative_spike
   - Expr: autoscaler_derivative_term > 0.2 * autoscaler_baseline (unitless)
   - For: 1m
   - Severity: ticket
   - Runbook: investigate recent policy changes or tenant labeling mismatches.

Query examples (PromQL)
----------------------

- 5s vs 30s token rate: 
  - tokens_5s = increase(tokens_total[5s]) / 5
  - tokens_30s = increase(tokens_total[30s]) / 30
- Oscillation rate: rate(autoscaler_scale_actions_total[5m])
- Eviction versus retry correlation: correlation_over_time(evictions_total, retries_total, 5m) (pseudo-query; implement with recording rules and join in Grafana).

Runbook snippet (operator steps on page)
---------------------------------------

1. Pager: receive page for autoscaler_oscillation_rate_high.
2. On-call: open Autoscaler-control-loop-overview dashboard.
3. Check scale-action-rate and eviction-rate graphs for the past 15 minutes.
4. If scale-ins were immediately followed by evictions and a retry spike, run: 
   - kubectl annotate pool/<pool-id> autoscaler.scale=paused --overwrite
   - curl -X POST https://internal-api/ops/pools/<pool-id>/min-replicas -d '{"min": <safe-count>}' 
5. Notify infra-autoscale and assign owner.
6. If manual pin applied, continue to monitor for 1 hour; if behavior stabilizes, migrate to scheduled remediation.

Checklist for future autoscaler rollouts
---------------------------------------

- Telemetry readiness: ensure tokens/sec recorded at 5s and 30s windows with dedicated recording rules.
- Canary readiness: synthetic canary capable of producing 1.5x mean load for 10s bursts.
- Control-loop simulation: local sims demonstrating damping across tenant profiles.
- Dashboard and alert coverage validated before feature flag flip.
- Rollout gating: success criteria defined (oscillation_rate < 0.3 actions/min and p99 latency within 5% of baseline).

Lessons learned
-------------

- LLM workloads are inherently bursty; control systems designed for web-traffic patterns (smooth, predictable) need re-evaluation.
- Observability should be designed around the control loop — not just per-metric. Visualizing estimator inputs, derivative terms, and action rates is critical.
- Tenant semantics matter: a one-size-fits-all stabilization window will fail.
- Small changes to forecasting heuristics can cascade when combined with eviction/retry behaviors.

Open action items (owner and due dates)
--------------------------------------

- Implement multi-timescale estimator and damped control law (owner: infra-autoscale — Diego Alvarez, due 2026-03-31).
- Add control-loop dashboards and recording rules (owner: eng-platform/dashboards — Priya Nair, due 2026-03-15).
- Add tenant profiling attributes and retroactive labeling for top 100 tenants (owner: product-platform — Evan Brooks, due 2026-04-15).
- Update operator runbooks with new CLI snippets and emergency pin procedure (owner: eng-platform/runbooks — Maya Chen, due 2026-03-10).
- Post-rollout gdoc checklist and handoff for SREs and Solutions Engineers (owner: eng-sre, due 2026-06-01).

Appendix: useful commands and test scripts
-----------------------------------------

- Pin autoscaler: kubectl annotate pool/<pool-id> autoscaler.scale=paused --overwrite
- Increase min replicas (internal API): 
  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' https://internal-api/ops/pools/<pool-id>/min-replicas -d '{"min": 4}'
- Synthetic canary runner (example): 
  python tools/canary_runner.py --target https://staging-runtime.example --rps 50 --burst 10 --duration 900

----------------
